As I said, it doesn't really have anything to do with Starship. Starship just provides a pretty formatted text to use, even if I add a functionality in Starship, called `--transient` (similar to `--right`, which at the moment is only supported by 3 out of 9 shells), it will be upto the shell to employ it.

+## TransientPrompt and TransientRightPrompt in Cmd
body:
I'm of a mind with @matchai on this, at least as far as this file goes. Most other sections here are 20-40 line vignettes with a fair bit of whitespace, for functionality that is at least present in one or two other shells. This is 70 lines of fairly-dense text (dense = "not a lot of whitespace", not "hard to read"), which inflates the file line count by almost 50%, for details of how to do a single feature in a single shell.

I think this is important documentation to have, I just don't think this file is the right place for it in this PR. There are a few places we could put this:

  - Abuse the per-platform nature of the `Advanced Installation` guide to add this there (though I don't think that's a great idea either)
  - Separate it into a GitHub discussion thread
  - If the other shells are going to have similarly-complex configuration for transient mode, we should probably collect the documentation for all of them in a common place.

@matchai At the rate we're going, we're going to need some way to formalize the support differences between shells. Do you think now is a good time to set that up?

body: I have reverted the commit

I just tried this, and it doesn't seem to work with a simple custom module of just `echo test`. I think the issue is that the command gets passed via stdin. See also the discussion in #2624 and #2629.
Does it work if you don't call this function at all (in `fn shell_command()`)? I will remove it then.
I believe the output will include the prompt in that case. It might be best to just `log::error!` and return if the shell is detected as `cmd`.

I think the reason the prompt gets shown is that cmd shell gets invoked without any params, i.e. `cmd echo test`. 

I have made the requested change.

I would prefer calling it `cmd` and I think this should include a troubleshooting suggestion.

```suggestion
            log::error!("Executing custom commands with the cmd shell is not currently supported. Please set a different shell with the \"shell\" option.");
```
